::: {.callout-important}
The AV Resource Portal's Data Dashboard was intended to show what publicly available data says about Autonomous Vehicle (AV) operations in San Francisco.  However, as described further in the Transparency section, limitations in the way data reports are designed, and redactions made by AV companies under privacy or confidential business information claims prevent the ability to present San Francisco data in most cases.  
:::

## Vehicle Miles Traveled

### By Company and Permit Type
Vehicle miles traveled (VMT) grew gradually from 2020 through 2023 when Waymo's VMT began to expand more rapidly.  Waymo has reported more VMT than other companies in each permit category for most of its history.  

Note that because it is possible that some of the VMT reported to DMV overlaps with VMT reported to CPUC, and because VMT has historically been reported to DMV only under testing permits, but not under deployment permits, it is not possible to sum across permit types.  

```{python}
#| label: fig1
#| column: page-right

fig4 = px.line(
    vmt_long.loc[:,['date','label','vmt']], 
    x='date', 
    y='vmt',
    color='label',
    color_discrete_map=company_permit_type_color_map,
    line_dash='label',
    line_dash_map=company_permit_type_dash_map,
    #height=500,
)

#fig4.update_layout(

fig4.show()
```

### Passenger Service and Deadheading
AV passenger services drive around empty in between trips.  This is called deadheading.  The CPUC categorizes passenger service into 3 phases: 

- Phase 1. A vehicle is empty and waiting for a passenger to request a ride
- Phase 2. Driving to pick up a passenger
- Phase 3. Transporting the passenger.  

Data by phase of service is reported to CPUC by companies operating under deployment permits.  Waymo is the only company currently operating driverless deployment passenger service.  Their VMT throughout California has grown consistently over time with only a few notable dips.  Cruise briefly operated driverless deployment passenger service before their permit was suspended and eventually revoked.  

```{python}
#| column: page-right
#| layout-nrow: 1

fig5 = px.area(
    period_vmt.loc[:,['company','date','period','period_vmt']], 
    x='date', 
    y='period_vmt',
    facet_col='company',
    color='period',
)
fig5.for_each_annotation(lambda a: a.update(text=a.text.split("=")[-1]))
fig5.show()
```

Person miles traveled (PMT) measures the distance that people travel.  An AV with 2 passengers that drives 1 VMT has 2 PMT.  One way to measure efficiency is PMT / VMT.  Driving alone, long considered the least-efficient mode has a PMT/VMT of 1.  Average PMT/VMT for a bus in San Francisco was 12.6

```{python}
#| column: page-right
#| layout-nrow: 1

synth_da = trip_long[['date']].drop_duplicates()
synth_da['label'] = 'Drive alone'
synth_da['pmt_over_vmt'] = 1
synth_bus = synth_da.copy()
synth_da['label'] = 'Bus'
synth_da['pmt_over_vmt'] = 12.6



fig7 = px.line(
    pd.concat(
        [trip_long.loc[:,['date','label','pmt_over_vmt']],
         synth_da,
         synth_bus
        ]
    ), 
    x='date', 
    y='pmt_over_vmt',
    color='label',
    color_discrete_map=company_permit_type_color_map,
    line_dash='label',
    line_dash_map=company_permit_type_dash_map,
)

fig7.update_layout(
    legend=dict(
        title='',
        orientation='h'
        )
    ).update_traces(
    visible="legendonly", 
    selector=lambda t: t.name in ["Bus"]
)

fig8 = px.line(
    trip_long.loc[:,['date','label','deadhead_rate']], 
    x='date', 
    y='deadhead_rate',
    color='label',
    color_discrete_map=company_permit_type_color_map,
    line_dash='label',
    line_dash_map=company_permit_type_dash_map,
)

fig8.update_layout(
    legend=dict(
        title='',
        orientation='h',
        ),
    yaxis=dict(
        range=(0,1)
    )
)



fig7.show()
fig8.show()
```

### Passenger Trips
Passenger trips are reported for companies operating under CPUC pilot and deployment permits.  Under pilot permits, a single statewide number is reported by month.  Under deployment permits, trips are reported by Census Tract.  In January 2025, Waymo (the only remaining deployment permittee) began redacting their trip Census Tracts, making it impossible to determine where in California they are providing trips.  

```{python}
#| column: page-right
#| layout-nrow: 1

fig1 = px.line(
    trip_long.loc[:,['date','label','trips']], 
    x='date', 
    y='trips',
    color='label',
    color_discrete_map=company_permit_type_color_map,
    line_dash='label',
    line_dash_map=company_permit_type_dash_map,
)
fig1.update_layout(
    legend=dict(
        title='',
        orientation='h'
        )
    )

fig3 = px.bar(
    trip_county_long.loc[:,['date','label','trips_start']], 
    x='date', 
    y='trips_start',
    color='label',
    color_discrete_map=company_county_color_map,
).update_traces(
    dict(marker_pattern_fgcolor=color_set_c_light[4],
         marker_pattern_shape='/',
         opacity=0.75
        ),
    selector=({'legendgroup':'Waymo Unidentified'}),
)

fig3.update_layout(
    legend=dict(
        title='',
        orientation='h'
        )
    )

fig1.show()
fig3.show()
``` 

### Geographic Distribution (2024 and earlier)
Based on geographic detail reported up through December 2024, AV trips occur in San Francisco and Los Angeles and are much more heavily concentrated in San Francisco.  Because Waymo no longer publicly reports any location information, it is not possible to say whether their growth from 2025 onward is from expansion into new markets or growth in existing markets.
